parsedVerdict.reasoning: ReturnBookUseCase.execute coordinates one use-case flow. It loads the loan through the LoanRepository port, gets the current time from the Clock port, hands the fine calculation to the domain FineCalculator service, and calls loan.close(now) and book.checkIn() on the domain entities. It then saves through the repository ports and maps the result to a DTO with toLoanDto. That is the expected role of an application-layer use case. The file has no persistence code, no transport or HTTP handling and no framework logic. Business rules (closing the loan, checking the book in, working out the fine) live in domain objects and are only called from here. The one borderline point is the constructor argument in `new FineCalculator(25)`. It fixes the fine rate in the use case, which is a policy value. Because the calculation stays in the domain service, this reads as configuring that service, not as business logic in the wrong layer. It's a minor design smell (better injected or placed in the domain), not a clear violation.
